title: Family still seeking answers
article: Tomorrow marks the one-year anniversary since Michael MacIsaac was shot dead in the streets in Ajax, Ont.
The 47-year-olds death has still not been justified, according to his sister Joanne MacIsaac and the rest of the family.
With the anniversary upon us, family members felt it was time to release all of the gathered information on the incident that left the Codroy Valley native dead.

To start, there was the forwarded 13-page letter sent to the Special Investigations Unit, based out of Mississauga. The letter contains significant information obtained by the family surrounding the details of Michaels death, in which they feel provides enough doubt to re-investigate the shooting and the death, which was in the hands of the Durham Regional Police.
The letter was dated July 7, 2014 and addressed to the director of the unit, Tony Loparco.

We believe the (unit's) investigation was woefully inadequate, lacked objectivity in assessing the facts, and contained material inaccuracies leading to an outcome not supported by the facts, wrote the family in the letter.
It is also the family's belief the officer who pulled the trigger should be charged with Michaels death and the Durham Regional Police should be investigated.
The morning of Dec. 2, 2013, Michael left his home naked and in a state of delirium, suffering from what the family said was an epileptic seizure and high fever.
His cry for help, the family maintains, was met with bullets.
Joanne said she has every reason to believe the police officer was in the wrong when it came to shooting her brother.
Witnesses told the family they saw Michael fall to the ground on his knees after the first shot. Two shots were fired.
Because of this, the family believes the officer is in clear violation of the Criminal Code, concerning self-defence laws.
Sufficient de-escalation methods or other options such as rubber bulletswere not employed, said Joanne, and the lethal second shot constituted the death of her brother.
A press release dated for June 3, 2014 wrote Loparco, the director of the unit, concluded there was no reasonable grounds to charge the officer in question with any criminal offence.
The release said 13 investigators and three forensic investigators were assigned to probe into the incident. Five officers and 17 civilian witnesses were interviewed.
Loparco was not made available for an interview.
The unit's communications specialist, Jasbir Brar, said the the unit is always willing to consider reopening its investigations in the event of new, material information.

The department stands by its June release and the information contained in it, and feel the job has been completed to the best of the unit's abilities even considering the facts the family presented to them in the 13-page letter.
- The family estimates the distance between the officer and Michael when the first shot was fired was 33-40 feet, not from close range. See - The difference in distance
- The family estimates the elapsed time from the arrival of the officer and the time he fired the first shot was less than 12 seconds. See - Time not tallying up: sister
- The second shot was unnecessary. See - Why another shot?
